rationaleAppend: Isaiah 35:2 (isaiah-woh wave I-5): hēmmāh yirʾû kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH hăḏar ʾĕlōhênû 'They shall see the glory of YHWH, the splendor of our God' (ASV 'the glory of Jehovah', JPS 1917 and NJPS 'the glory of the LORD', checked 2026-11-26). The verse sets kāḇôḏ beside hāḏār 'splendor' (isaiah-woh overlay hadar-splendor-isaiah) and uses kāḇôḏ in the same verse of Lebanon (overlay kavod-nondivine-glory-isaiah). The isaiah-woh commentary carries a separately labelled speculative reception note on this verse; the entry's claim is unchanged.

Isaiah 35:2 (isaiah-woh wave I-5): pārōaḥ tip̄raḥ 'It shall blossom abundantly' (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS, checked 2026-11-26); the construction with the verb prḥ, rendered by the adverb as the entry prescribes.

changes.wohChoice: One English root for the gʾl family: 'redeem' (verb), 'redeemer' (gōʾēl; capitalised 'Redeemer' as a divine title in Isaiah: 'your Redeemer', Isa 43:14; 44:6, 24; 48:17; 54:5, 8), 'redemption' (gəʾullâ). Lev 25: 'his redeemer who is nearest to him' (25:25; ASV 'his kinsman that is next unto him'), 'a redemption for the land' (25:24), 'redeem' (25:25-54 passim). Where gəʾullâ denotes the kin group that holds the right of redemption, it is rendered by its referent: 'the men of your kindred' (Ezek 11:15, ʾanšê ḡəʾullāṯeḵā). The verb pāḏâ 'ransom, redeem' (Ex 13:13-15; Num 18:15-17; 1 Kgs 1:29; Isa 1:27; 29:22) also takes 'redeem' in the corpus and is distinguished in commentary, with one context clause: where pāḏâ stands in parallel with gāʾal, pāḏâ takes 'ransom', so that the two roots keep distinct English words (Isa 35:9-10 gəʾûlîm 'the redeemed' … pəḏûyê YHWH 'the ransomed of YHWH'; proposed for the duplicate Isa 51:10-11; the same distinction as ASV Jer 31:11; Hos 13:14; Ps 69:19 [ASV 69:18]; Lev 27:27). The formula of Gen 48:16 is governed by ha-mal-akh-ha-go-el-mi-kol-ra-unified-theophanic-redeemer-formula.

rationaleAppend: Context clause for pāḏâ (isaiah-woh wave I-5, chapter 35 Editor; awaiting founder ruling). The default 'redeem' for pāḏâ rests on the ASV, which prints 'redeem' for the finite verb (Isa 1:27; 29:22). The ASV does not keep that default where the two roots meet. At Isa 35:9-10 it has 'the redeemed' for gəʾûlîm and 'the ransomed of Jehovah' for pəḏûyê YHWH, and the same at 51:10-11; at Jer 31:11 it has 'Jehovah hath ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him', at Hos 13:14 'I will ransom them … I will redeem them', and the same distinction holds at Ps 69:19 (ASV 69:18) and Lev 27:27 (bible-api.com, checked 2026-11-26; Ps 69 and Lev 27 confirmed by the Reviewer). The clause therefore rests on ASV's practice. It does not rest on the versions in general: KJV reverses the pair at Isa 51:10-11 and Jer 31:11 (Reviewer, checked), although JPS 1917, KJV and NJPS all print 'the ransomed' at Isa 35:10 (Sefaria API v3 and bible-api.com, checked). The clause remains pending the founder's ruling. Applying 'redeem' at 35:10 would give one English word to two roots in adjacent verses, which is the merging this entry's own rationale says commentary must undo ('commentary distinguishes the two where they meet'). The clause keeps the corpus default and the stable Isaiah sites (1:27; 29:22) unchanged and adds only the parallel case. 'Ransom' is a standard gloss of pāḏâ (BDB, HALOT; recalled), so the claim stays direct. ISA-35:9 is listed for gəʾûlîm (Qal passive participle of gāʾal) and ISA-35:10 for the context clause.
